query: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi has high saturation magnetization but a low coercive field, and reported single-phase fcc high-entropy alloys derived from it have coercive fields no greater than 100 Oe in the reported magnetic measurements. What single intervention could overcome this coercivity limitation? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, the predicted change relative to single-phase fcc FeCoNi or a matched derivative, the relevant compositional, structural, and measurement boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with an explicit falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: Rapid quenching via arc melting on a water-cooled copper hearth induces the formation of a fine-scale secondary C14 Laves phase in FeCoNi alloys, which increases magnetic domain wall pinning and thus significantly enhances the coercivity compared to the conventional single-phase fcc structure.
generation.material_initial_state: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi or a compositionally matched high-entropy alloy with coercivity ≤100 Oe.
generation.intervention: Process the alloy using rapid quenching by arc melting on a water-cooled copper hearth to promote the nucleation of a secondary C14 Laves phase.
generation.conditions: Maintain identical overall composition for both sample sets. Compare samples processed with rapid quenching to those processed via conventional slower cooling under controlled atmosphere and room temperature measurements.
generation.structural_mediator: Nucleation of a minor, finely dispersed C14 Laves phase within the fcc matrix.
generation.mechanism: The secondary C14 Laves phase forms discrete precipitates that act as pinning sites for magnetic domain walls, impeding their motion and thereby increasing the coercive field.
generation.predicted_outcome: The rapidly quenched sample will exhibit a coercive field exceeding 100 Oe (i.e., significantly enhanced relative to the single-phase fcc sample) due to additional domain wall pinning.
generation.baseline: Conventionally processed single-phase fcc FeCoNi high-entropy alloy with coercivity ≤100 Oe.
generation.boundary: The conclusion is applicable to FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloys with identical compositions, processed under precisely controlled thermal conditions, and measured under standard magnetic characterization conditions (e.g., room temperature, using vibrating sample magnetometry).
generation.uncertainty: The magnitude and uniformity of the C14 phase formation and its exact effect on coercivity remain uncertain. Variability in processing parameters and microstructure-property relationships may affect the precise coercivity enhancement.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of compositionally matched FeCoNi high-entropy alloy samples. Process one set by rapid quenching via arc melting on a water-cooled copper hearth and the other set by a conventional slower cooling method. Use X-ray diffraction and electron microscopy to identify the presence of any secondary C14 Laves phase. Measure the magnetic hysteresis loops using a vibrating sample magnetometer to determine the coercive fields.
measurements: VSM for coercivity (magnetic hysteresis loop) measurement
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the rapidly quenched samples do not show a significant increase in coercivity (i.e., remain at or below 100 Oe) and no additional C14 Laves phase is detected compared to the conventionally processed samples, then the hypothesis is falsified.
